parts.gloss: that which is of greater hardness

words.gloss: that which is of greater hardness

literal: The suffering of poverty, 'by begging we shall cure', thinking, than that hardness of mind, of greater hardness, there is nothing.
translation: There is no greater hardness of heart than the determination of those who think they can cure the misery of poverty by begging.
modern: வறுமையின் துன்பத்தை பிறரிடம் இரந்து கேட்டுப் போக்கிக் கொள்வோம் என்று நினைக்கும் மனவலிமையைக் காட்டிலும் கொடுமையான வன்னெஞ்சம் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet exposes the shameless mindset of those who choose to beg. The poet uses the word 'vanmai' (strength/hardness of mind) ironically to describe the resolve of a person who decides to cure the misery of poverty ('inmai iṭumpai') by begging ('irantu tīrvām'). The poet then declares that there is nothing more hard-hearted or cruel ('vanpāṭṭatu il') than this specific kind of mental strength. To lose one's self-respect and rely on begging, rather than facing poverty with dignity or labor, is presented as the ultimate form of insensitivity.
